To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

neutron irradiation causes a decrease of carrier mobility, an increase of the deep-level defect density, and a decrease of the free-carrier density in SiC JFETs at temperatures ranging from RT to 300/sup 0/C. The

neutron irradiation at RT induces a deep-level trap in 6H-SiC which is responsible for the observed carrier removal, and that the neutron-induced carrier removal rate is approximately a linear function of temperature.
neutron-induced carrier removal rates in SiC JFETs increase with increasing temperature from RT to 300/sup o/C.
